correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RESULT.md lines 51–69. Each b is labeled by its number i of preceding a's; these labels are weakly increasing and their multiplicities uniquely specify the word. Their sum is C. A set of occupied interior gaps uniquely determines the maximum possible number of alternating b selections: each gap supplies at most one, and taking one from each leaves an a on either end and between consecutive choices. Independent gap multiplicities yield (1), and setting z=1 gives [u^(B-j)](1-u)^(-j-2) times binomial(A-1,j), including B<j, A=1 and C=0. In the stable regime C<A, B>=C, the positive labels give unrestricted partitions, so J is their number of distinct sizes. The minimum area for j sizes is triangular, and any excess may be added to the largest distinct part. For fixed r>=2 the avoidance numerator lies between 1 and a polynomial in C; Hardy–Ramanujan then gives the logarithmic estimate. Removing one part of size k gives the exact mean. For k<=C^(3/5), the partition ratio is exp(-pi k/sqrt(6C))(1+o(1)) uniformly by Taylor expansion; monotonicity bounds the remaining sum by C times an exponentially small ratio in C^(1/10). This gives the asserted mean constant. Independently, at C=10 the four one-size partitions correspond to divisors of 10; two sizes give 22 by positive multiplicity counts, and four sizes force 1,2,3,4, leaving 15 three-size partitions. Both supplied checkers and their stored outputs were inspected, not executed; their bounded tests are supplementary.

evidence: When A>C and B>=C, the identical gap law specializes to the unrestricted distinct-size mark on partitions of C.
The first marked moment in that unrestricted product has GF (sum_{k>=1}q^k) times the ordinary partition GF; the support is the triangular lower bound with excess put into the largest part.
For fixed r the marked coefficient count below r is between 1 and a fixed polynomial in C, so dividing by p(C) gives the displayed logarithmic scale.
